answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to forge and cheap to verify: each agent must stake a deposit that is slashed when fraud is proven, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real money instead of nothing. That stake is then bound to a lasting record, the way a ferrous tool keeps its shape under load, and reputation accrues only through completed work over time, like marble that gains value once it is quarried, cut, and shown to last. Throwaway accounts buy no trust.
